title: Real Time Edge
motto: Edge inference is the discipline of getting a 90-accuracy model to run at 30 fps on a device with 2 GB of RAM. Every percentage point of accuracy is traded against milliseconds of latency.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: Edge inference is the discipline of getting a 90-accuracy model to run at 30 fps on a device with 2 GB of RAM. Every percentage point of accuracy is traded against milliseconds of latency.

steps.title: The problem
cards: A training-time vision model is a floating-point monster. 100M parameters, 10 GFLOPs per forward pass, 2 GB of VRAM. None of that fits on a phone, a car's infotainment unit, an industrial camera, or a drone. Shipping a vision system means fitting the same predictions into a budget that is 100x smaller.

Three knobs do most of the work: model choice (a smaller architecture with the same recipe), quantisation (INT8 instead of FP32), and the inference runtime (ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, Core ML, TFLite). Getting them right is the difference between a demo that runs on a workstation and a product that ships on a $30 camera module.

This lesson sets up the measurement discipline first (you cannot optimise what you cannot measure), then walks the three knobs. The goal is not to learn every edge runtime but to know what levers exist and how to verify each one does what you think.
